docs.title: Definition of Done
docs.text:
• The task's done_when check passes.
  • Tests exist for every scenario and pass.
  • The quality gate reports pass or skipped (never fail).
  • No OPEN: item remains.

docs.title: Contract: tenant read guard (path 1, accepted)
docs.text: Caller tenant T = _resolve_tenant(tenant_id), the write-guard helper, unchanged. T can be None. T is never "". Readable: T set gives tenant_id = T OR tenant_id IS NULL. T is None gives tenant_id IS NULL. Owned (write and delete): tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM T. Signatures and return types do not change. The protocol src/core/plugins/protocols/relational_db.py does not change.

docs.title: Callers (checked at bc02a46)
docs.text:
• src/: no callers. Only definitions (protocol, postgres.py). src/core/security/rbac.py has an unrelated delete_document(document_id, role).
  • tests/: tests/integration/plugins/test_postgres.py, test_postgres_status_guard.py, test_postgres_tenant_guard.py, tests/integration/test_reject_document.py, tests/integration/tasks/test_fetch_close_store.py, tests/factories/plugins.py. A test that reads a tenant row with no tenant, or deletes a row of another tenant or a shared row as a tenant, breaks. Task 1 checks each one.

docs.title: get_document(document_id: str, tenant_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None
docs.text: Query: SELECT ... WHERE id = :id AND <readable>. Inputs: document_id (str), tenant_id (optional, "" counts as not given). Outputs: the row as doc_to_dict, or None when the row is missing or not readable. Errors: none new. Database errors pass through (unchanged).

docs.title: search_documents(query: str, *, limit: int = 10, tenant_id: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
docs.text: Query: the existing ILIKE on title or content, AND <readable>, ORDER BY last_updated DESC LIMIT :limit. Outputs: up to limit readable rows (own and shared), newest first. Foreign rows are omitted before the limit. Errors: none new.

docs.title: get_recent_changes(*, since: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
docs.text: Query: <readable>, AND last_updated > since when since is set, newest first. No LIMIT (unchanged, follow-up). Outputs: all readable rows that match. Errors: none new. A bad since string raises as today (_parse_dt).

docs.title: delete_document(document_id: str, tenant_id: str | None = None) -> None
docs.text: Statement: DELETE FROM legal_document WHERE id = :id AND <owned>, then commit. One atomic statement. Outputs: an owned row is deleted. A missing, foreign or (for a tenant caller) shared id deletes nothing. All return None. Errors: none new. It does not raise StoreDocumentNotFoundError. It does not call on_document_deleted (unchanged, only reject calls it).

docs.title: Private helpers (postgres.py)
docs.text:
• _readable_by(tenant: str | None) -> ColumnElement[bool]: read predicate. or_(LegalDocument.tenant_id == tenant, LegalDocument.tenant_id.is_(None)) when tenant is set, else LegalDocument.tenant_id.is_(None). No error.
  • _owned_by(tenant: str | None) -> ColumnElement[bool]: write predicate. LegalDocument.tenant_id.is_not_distinct_from(tenant). _owned_row_for_update and delete_document use it. No error.
  • _require_writable keeps its Python check for save_document (unchanged).

docs.title: Guard limit
docs.text: A caller with no tenant can delete every shared row. The store does not check the role. Caller RBAC (admin, ADR-0013) is the only guard on this path until RLS exists.

docs.title: Decision: tenant read guard
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner, 2026-11-18). Path 1, with the owner answers to Q1 and Q2.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: get_document, search_documents, get_recent_changes and delete_document accept tenant_id and ignore it. A tenant can read and delete a foreign row by id. legal_document has no RLS. No code in src/ calls these four methods today. Only tests call them. Size S (one module, no schema change), so two paths were compared.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1, predicates in the SQL of every statement, Core delete.
  • Path 2, ORM load and a Python check for single rows, SQL filter for lists.
Row Path 1 Path 2 Fit to constraints (T1-T6) Full T3 partly: rule in Python and SQL Failure modes F1-F4 Met Met Race between check and delete None (one statement) Gap, but no leak Foreign row loaded into memory No Yes Complexity 2 helpers, one per rule 1 helper, two forms of one rule Effort S S Main risk Core delete skips ORM cascades (none today) Python and SQL rules drift apart

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 1, with these rules. - D1. Tenant: T = _resolve_tenant(tenant_id), the write-guard helper, unchanged. - D2. Read predicate _readable_by(T): T set gives tenant_id = T OR tenant_id IS NULL. T is None gives tenant_id IS NULL. A Python branch picks the form, because a B-tree index cannot use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (dba). Used by get_document, search_documents, get_recent_changes. - D3. Write predicate _owned_by(T): tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM T, the write-guard rule. Used by _owned_row_for_update and delete_document. A tenant cannot delete a shared row. - D4. delete_document returns None. It runs one atomic DELETE ... WHERE id = :id AND _owned_by(T). A missing or foreign id is a no-op, with no error. Reasons: the public contract stays, foreign and missing give the same answer, and a Celery retry does not fail. The write guard set no precedent for delete (it only kept the existing KeyError of update_document).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A tenant cannot read, list or delete a foreign row through the store.
  • A tenant reads the shared corpus but cannot delete or write it.
  • A no-tenant caller reads only shared rows, and can delete every shared row. Caller RBAC (admin) is the only guard until RLS exists.
  • A caller cannot tell a failed delete from a delete of a missing id.
  • Reads and writes now use different rules. The helper names make the difference clear.
  • Follow-ups: see "Out of scope / follow-ups" in requirements.md.

docs.title: Requirements: tenant read guard
docs.text:
Scope: PostgreSQLStore.get_document, search_documents, get_recent_changes and delete_document in src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py.

Source of facts: the code at commit bc02a46. The owner fixed the rules below on 2026-11-18.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• G1. A tenant cannot read or delete a document of another tenant through the store. This is a charter item ("tenant leak tests") for the MVP (planning date 2027-02-28).
  • G2. A caller cannot learn that a foreign document exists from a read or a delete. A foreign row gives the same answer as a missing row.
  • G3. Tenant users can read the shared corpus (charter: "shared documents, per-tenant data").
  • G4. Close the read and delete follow-up of the tenant write guard before RLS work starts.

Decided: the store, not its callers, enforces the read rule and the delete rule.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• T1. Python 3.13, SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM, PostgreSQL. No new dependency. No schema change and no migration.
  • T2. Reuse _resolve_tenant without change. The tenant is the tenant_id argument, else get_current_tenant(). "" counts as None.
  • T3. Two predicates, each with one source:
  • Read predicate: tenant T set gives tenant_id = T OR tenant_id IS NULL. T is None gives tenant_id IS NULL. A Python branch picks the form. Do not use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM for reads, because a B-tree index cannot use it (dba).
  • Write predicate: tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM T, the write-guard rule, unchanged. _owned_row_for_update and delete_document use it.
  • T4. Keep the public signatures and return types of the four calls. The protocol in src/core/plugins/protocols/relational_db.py does not change.
  • T5. Celery prefork workers do not carry the contextvar. They pass tenant_id as an argument.
  • T6. Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, pytest. Integration tests run on the Docker PostgreSQL. Coverage and mutation gates as in CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• E1. Read rule: a tenant caller sees its own rows and shared rows. A no-tenant caller sees only shared rows. A foreign row is never visible.
  • E2. Delete rule: the write-guard rule (NULL is equal to NULL). A tenant deletes only its own rows. A tenant cannot delete a shared row. A no-tenant caller deletes only shared rows.
  • E3. A no-tenant caller can delete every shared row. Caller RBAC (admin role, ADR-0013) is the only guard on this path until RLS exists.
  • E4. Argument and context both set and different: the argument wins.
  • E5. Empty-string tenant in the argument: falls back to the context tenant. It never widens access.
  • E6. search_documents with limit: the limit applies after the tenant filter.
  • E7. get_recent_changes with since: the tenant filter and the since filter both apply.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• F1. get_document of a foreign id returns None, the same as a missing id.
  • F2. search_documents and get_recent_changes omit foreign rows.
  • F3. delete_document of a missing, foreign or (for a tenant caller) shared id is a no-op. It returns None and raises no error. The row stays unchanged.
  • F4. No log line contains the caller tenant, the row tenant or the document id.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• M1. 100% of the QA cases pass on the Docker PostgreSQL.
  • M2. get_document: the result for a foreign id and a missing id is equal (None) in 100% of the cases.
  • M3. 0 foreign rows in the results of search_documents and get_recent_changes. Shared rows are in the results of a tenant caller.
  • M4. 0 deleted foreign rows, and 0 shared rows deleted by a tenant caller. The kept row has all 10 doc_to_dict fields unchanged.
  • M5. 0 regressions in the existing store tests (unit and Docker integration suite).
  • M6. Coverage and mutation scores on the changed lines meet the CONTRIBUTING.md gates (no gate lowered).

docs.title: Out of scope / follow-ups
docs.text:
• RLS on legal_document.
  • No index and no migration now. legal_document.tenant_id has no index. Add (tenant_id, last_updated DESC) with the RLS migration.
  • get_recent_changes has no LIMIT. It returns all visible rows.
  • The RLS session hook (_set_tenant_setting) sets the tenant from the context, not from the resolved argument. The RLS work must close this gap.
  • Do not copy the setting = '' policy pattern of tenants and users to legal_document.
  • reject stays global (no tenant check).
  • Server-generated ids only.

docs.title: Tasks: tenant read guard (path 1, accepted)
docs.text:
Gate before build: the solution-architect checks contract.md against the current code.

  1. Check callers. Read each test caller listed in contract.md. Find each call that reads a tenant row with no tenant or with another tenant, or deletes a foreign or shared row as a tenant. Done when: the list is in the PR body, and each such test has a fix in task 4.
  2. Write unit tests first in tests/unit/plugins/test_postgres_tenant_guard.py, with FakeSession from tests/fakes/postgres_session.py. Assert on the compiled SQL in session.statements:
  3. With a tenant, get_document, search_documents and get_recent_changes send tenant_id = :T OR tenant_id IS NULL. With no tenant they send tenant_id IS NULL. None of them sends IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.
  4. delete_document sends one DELETE with tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM and commits once.
  5. The argument wins over the context. An argument "" falls back to the context.
  6. search_documents has the tenant filter before LIMIT. Done when: the tests fail on main.
  7. Write integration tests first in tests/integration/plugins/test_postgres_tenant_guard.py, on the Docker PostgreSQL:
  8. A tenant sees its own rows and shared rows, and not foreign rows, in get_document, search_documents and get_recent_changes.
  9. get_document of a foreign id returns None, the same as a missing id.
  10. A no-tenant caller sees only shared rows.
  11. With limit=1, search_documents returns an own row when a newer foreign row exists.
  12. A tenant cannot delete a shared row or a foreign row. All 10 doc_to_dict fields of the kept row stay unchanged. The call returns None with no error.
  13. A tenant deletes its own row. A no-tenant caller deletes a shared row and cannot delete a tenant row. Done when: the tests fail on main for every case except "missing id returns None", "tenant sees shared rows", "tenant deletes own row" and "no-tenant caller deletes a shared row".
  14. Add _readable_by and _owned_by. Use _owned_by in _owned_row_for_update and delete_document, and _readable_by in the three read calls (see contract.md). Update the four docstrings and state the guard limit. Fix the tests from task 1. Done when: the tests of tasks 2 and 3 pass, and the existing store tests pass.
  15. Run the quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, pytest -m "not integration", the Docker suite, and the coverage and mutation gates. Done when: all pass with no gate lowered.

Order: tasks 1, 2 and 3 in parallel, then 4, then 5. Follow-ups: see "Out of scope / follow-ups" in requirements.md.

docs.title: Path 1: predicates in the SQL of every statement
docs.text: Lens: the tenant filter lives in the SQL WHERE of each statement. Each predicate has one source.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• _readable_by(tenant): read predicate. tenant set gives or_(tenant_id == tenant, tenant_id.is_(None)). None gives tenant_id.is_(None).
  • _owned_by(tenant): write predicate, tenant_id.is_not_distinct_from(tenant). _owned_row_for_update uses it.
  • get_document: select(LegalDocument).where(id == :id, _readable_by(T)), then scalar_one_or_none(). Replaces session.get.
  • search_documents and get_recent_changes: add _readable_by(T) to the existing WHERE.
  • delete_document: delete(LegalDocument).where(id == :id, _owned_by(T)) in one transaction. Zero rows is a no-op. reject already uses a Core delete, so this is not a new pattern.

docs.title: Fit
docs.text:
• T2, T3, E1, E2: met. The tenant is a bound parameter in SQL.
  • E6: met. The database applies LIMIT after the filter.
  • F1-F3: met. Check and delete are one atomic statement, so there is no race window.

Effort: S. About 20 changed lines and two small helpers.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
1. The Core delete skips ORM cascades and before_delete hooks. Today LegalDocument has none in use (the reject path deletes the same way).
  2. get_document no longer uses the identity map. This has no effect, because each call opens a new session.

docs.title: Path 2: ORM load, then a Python check for single rows
docs.text: Lens: keep session.get for single-row calls and check ownership in Python, as save_document does with _require_writable. Lists filter in SQL.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• _owns(row, tenant) -> bool: row is not None and row.tenant_id == tenant. _require_writable calls it, so the Python rule exists once.
  • get_document: session.get, then _owns. A foreign row returns None.
  • delete_document: session.get, then _owns, then session.delete(row) and commit. A foreign row is a no-op.
  • search_documents and get_recent_changes: add LegalDocument.tenant_id.is_not_distinct_from(T) to the WHERE (a list cannot be filtered in Python without breaking limit).

docs.title: Fit
docs.text:
• T2, E1: met.
  • T3: partly met. The rule exists twice: once in Python (_owns) and once in SQL (lists and _owned_row_for_update). A test must keep the two in step.
  • F1-F3: met. The delete has a gap between load and delete, but tenant_id cannot change through the store, so the gap does not leak.

Effort: S. About 20 changed lines and one small helper.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
1. Two forms of one rule (Python and SQL) can drift apart.
  2. A foreign row is loaded into the session before the check. It is not returned, but it is in process memory.
  3. A delete of a row that a concurrent call already removed gives a SQLAlchemy warning on flush, not an error.

docs.title: Contract: tenant write guard (path 1, accepted)
docs.text: Caller tenant T = _resolve_tenant(tenant_id). T can be None. T is never "". A row is writable when row.tenant_id == T (None == None is true). NotFound = StoreDocumentNotFoundError(KeyError), str(exc) == "Document not found: <id>". Row locks hold until commit or rollback.

docs.title: PostgreSQLStore.save_document(document: dict[str, Any], tenant_id: str | None = None) -> str
docs.text:
Load: session.get(LegalDocument, id, with_for_update=True), then _require_writable.

Inputs: - document: needs title, content, source, source_url for an insert. id optional. status and tenant_id keys are ignored. - tenant_id: optional. Overrides the context. "" counts as not given.

Outputs: - No id, or id with no row: inserts a row with tenant_id=T, status=needs_review. Returns the id. Sets document["id"]. - id of a writable row: copies allowlisted fields (apply_update). Keeps status, tenant_id, id. Returns the id. - Logs one warning with the operation name and the dropped key names only (insert: status, tenant_id; upsert: status, tenant_id, unknown keys). No document id, no values.

Errors: - NotFound: id of a row that is not writable. No write, no commit. document is not changed. - NotFound: StaleDataError on flush. The session rolls back. - KeyError (bare): a required insert field is missing (unchanged). - sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: concurrent insert of the same new id (unchanged, kept by a test).

docs.title: PostgreSQLStore.update_document(document_id: str, document: dict[str, Any], tenant_id: str | None = None) -> None
docs.text:
Load: _owned_row_for_update(session, document_id, T). It runs SELECT ... WHERE id = :id AND tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM :T FOR UPDATE. It locks only an eligible row, so a foreign update never waits on the lock of the owner.

Inputs: document_id (str), document (partial fields), tenant_id (optional, "" counts as not given). Outputs: allowlisted fields are copied and committed. status, tenant_id, unknown keys are dropped. One warning logs the operation name and the key names only. Errors: - NotFound: no row, or the row is not writable. Same type and text for both. No write, no commit. - NotFound: StaleDataError on flush. The session rolls back.

docs.title: StoreDocumentNotFoundError
docs.text:
• Base: KeyError (was LookupError). Still a LookupError.
  • __str__ returns the message without quotes.
  • reject keeps its current behaviour and text.

docs.title: Private helpers (postgres.py)
docs.text:
• _resolve_tenant(tenant_id: str | None) -> str | None: arg = tenant_id or None. t = arg if arg is not None else get_current_tenant(). Returns t or None. No payload input. No error.
  • _owned_row_for_update(session: Session, document_id: str, tenant: str | None) -> LegalDocument: returns the locked row, or raises NotFound when no eligible row exists.
  • _require_writable(row: LegalDocument | None, document_id: str, tenant: str | None) -> LegalDocument: used by save_document. Returns the row, or raises NotFound.

docs.title: mappers.apply_update(row, document) -> list[str]
docs.text: No change. It never writes tenant_id, status or id.

docs.title: Guard limit
docs.text: A caller with no tenant can write every shared row. The store does not check the role. Caller RBAC (admin, ADR-0013) is the only guard on this path until RLS exists.

docs.title: Decision: tenant write guard
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner, 2026-11-18). Path 1, all five defaults, and the dba changes.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: save_document lets a payload tenant_id pick the tenant on insert. save_document (upsert) and update_document load rows by id with no tenant filter. legal_document has no RLS. Size S (one module, no schema change), so two paths were compared.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1, ORM load-then-check: load under a row lock, then a Python ownership check, then apply_update.
  • Path 2, set-based conditional SQL: UPDATE ... WHERE tenant IS NOT DISTINCT FROM and INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE.
Row Path 1 Path 2 Fit to constraints (T1-T6) Full. No new SQL dialect use. Full. PostgreSQL-only SQL. Failure modes F1-F3 Met Met Race between check and write Closed by row locks (dba change) Closed (one statement) Same-id insert race (F5) IntegrityError (unchanged) Changed: update or not-found Complexity 3 small helpers, apply_update unchanged New values builder, 2 Core statements, empty-SET fallback Effort S M Main risk Guard lives in Python only ORM hooks and type coercion skipped

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 1, with these rules. - Tenant: _resolve_tenant changes "" to None, then uses the tenant_id argument if not None, else get_current_tenant() (also "" to None). Payload tenant_id is dropped and logged by name. - Load in update_document: _owned_row_for_update selects by id AND tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM tenant, FOR UPDATE. It locks only an eligible row. - Load in save_document: session.get(LegalDocument, id, with_for_update=True), then the ownership check. - Ownership: row.tenant_id == tenant, NULL == NULL. Tenant rows are writable only by that tenant. Shared rows are writable only with no tenant. - Error: StoreDocumentNotFoundError, base changed to KeyError, plain __str__. update_document gives the same type and text Document not found: <id> for missing and foreign rows. StaleDataError on flush maps to the same error. - Upsert of a foreign id raises. It never inserts a new id and never overwrites. The payload dict stays unchanged. - Argument and context differ: the argument wins. - The dropped-key warning logs the operation name and key names only.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The race between check and write is closed. A foreign update never waits on the lock of the owner.
  • update_document raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError instead of bare KeyError. except KeyError still works.
  • reject callers that catch StoreDocumentNotFoundError or LookupError keep working.
  • A caller with no tenant can write every shared row. Caller RBAC (admin role) is the only guard until RLS exists.
  • Two inserts of the same new id still race. The second raises IntegrityError, and a test keeps this.
  • Residual oracle: on save_document, an unknown caller-chosen id inserts, and a foreign id raises (accepted risk).
  • Follow-ups (not in this task): server-generated ids only (no caller-chosen ids). Tenant filter on get_document, search_documents, get_recent_changes, delete_document. RLS on legal_document.

docs.title: QA cases: tenant write guard
docs.text: Setup: rows A1 (tenant A), B1 (tenant B), S1 (shared, NULL). "Unchanged" means all 10 doc_to_dict fields are equal before and after (M2). All cases run on the Docker PostgreSQL.

docs.title: QA-1
docs.text: Covers: T2, E3 Given the context tenant is A When save_document inserts a new row with payload tenant_id="B" Then the row has tenant_id="A" and the warning names tenant_id

docs.title: QA-2
docs.text: Covers: T2, E1c Given no context tenant and no argument When save_document inserts a new row with payload tenant_id="B" Then the row has tenant_id NULL

docs.title: QA-3
docs.text: Covers: E4, F2, M3a Given the context tenant is A When save_document({"id": "B1", ...}) runs Then it raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError with the text Document not found: B1 and no new row exists

docs.title: QA-4
docs.text: Covers: F1 Given the context tenant is A When update_document("B1", {"title": "x"}) runs Then it raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError and B1 is unchanged

docs.title: QA-5
docs.text: Covers: G2, M3 Given the context tenant is A When update_document runs for B1 and for an id with no row Then both raise the same type with the text Document not found: <id>

docs.title: QA-6
docs.text: Covers: E1a Given the context tenant is A When update_document("S1", ...) and save_document({"id": "S1", ...}) run Then both raise StoreDocumentNotFoundError and S1 is unchanged

docs.title: QA-7
docs.text: Covers: E1b Given no tenant When update_document("A1", {"title": "x"}) runs Then it raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError and A1 is unchanged

docs.title: QA-8
docs.text: Covers: E1, E1d Given no tenant When update_document("S1", {"title": "x"}) runs Then the title is x and tenant_id stays NULL

docs.title: QA-9
docs.text: Covers: E2 Given the context tenant is B and the argument is A When update_document("A1", {"title": "x"}, tenant_id="A") runs Then the title is x

docs.title: QA-10
docs.text: Covers: T2, F6 Given the context tenant is A When update_document("A1", {"title": "x", "tenant_id": "B"}) runs Then the title is x, tenant_id stays A, and the warning holds the operation name and tenant_id, but no value and no document id

docs.title: QA-11
docs.text: Covers: E5 Given the context tenant is A and the argument is "" When update_document("S1", {"title": "x"}, tenant_id="") runs Then it raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError, S1 is unchanged, and update_document("A1", {"title": "y"}, tenant_id="") sets the title of A1 to y

docs.title: QA-12
docs.text: Covers: F3 Given a StoreDocumentNotFoundError is raised When an except KeyError handler wraps the call Then the handler catches it, str(exc) has no quotes, and isinstance(exc, LookupError) is true

docs.title: QA-13
docs.text: Covers: F2 Given the context tenant is A and a payload dict {"id": "B1", "title": "x", ...} When save_document raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError Then B1 is unchanged and the payload dict is equal to a copy taken before the call

docs.title: QA-14
docs.text: Covers: F5 Given two sessions on two database backends and one new id with no row When session 1 runs the lookup and the insert and keeps the transaction open, and session 2 runs the lookup (it misses) and the insert in a second thread And the test waits until pg_blocking_pids of backend 2 contains backend 1, then commits session 1 Then session 1 returns the id and session 2 raises IntegrityError

docs.title: QA-15
docs.text: Covers: F7 Given the context tenant is A and the flush of an A1 update raises StaleDataError When update_document("A1", {"title": "x"}) runs Then it raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError with the text Document not found: A1 and the session rolls back

docs.title: QA-16
docs.text: Covers: T7 Given session 1 holds the lock on A1 through an open update_document transaction for tenant A When update_document("A1", {"title": "x"}) runs for tenant B in session 2 Then session 2 raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError at once, without a wait on the lock of session 1

docs.title: Requirements: tenant write guard
docs.text:
Scope: PostgreSQLStore.save_document and PostgreSQLStore.update_document in src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py, and mappers.apply_update. Out of scope: RLS on legal_document, tenant filters on read paths (get_document, search_documents, get_recent_changes) and on delete_document.

Source of facts: the code at commit ba4286a and the follow-ups in docs/design/document-status-guard/review.md. The owner accepted every default below, and the dba changes, on 2026-11-18.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• G1. A tenant cannot change or claim a document of another tenant through the store. This is a charter item ("tenant leak tests") for the MVP (planning date 2027-02-28).
  • G2. A caller cannot learn that a document of another tenant exists from the update path. The answer for a foreign row is the same as for a missing row.
  • G3. Close the two security follow-ups (medium) from the document status guard review before RLS work starts.

Decided: the store, not its callers, enforces the write rule.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• T1. Python 3.13, SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM, PostgreSQL. No new dependency. No schema change and no migration.
  • T2. The tenant comes only from the tenant_id argument or get_current_tenant(). A payload tenant_id never picks the tenant. Rule: first change "" to None in the argument, then tenant = argument if argument is not None else get_current_tenant(), then change "" to None in the result.
  • T3. Reuse the existing error type. StoreDocumentNotFoundError exists (base LookupError). update_document raises KeyError for a missing id today. Callers that catch KeyError must keep working.
  • T4. legal_document.tenant_id is nullable. NULL means a shared document (charter: shared documents, per-tenant data).
  • T5. Celery prefork workers do not carry the contextvar. They pass tenant_id as an argument (core/security/tenant.py note).
  • T6. Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, pytest. Integration tests run on the Docker PostgreSQL. Coverage and mutation gates as in CONTRIBUTING.md.
  • T7. Row locks:
  • update_document selects the row by id AND tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM tenant, with FOR UPDATE (helper _owned_row_for_update). It locks only an eligible row. A foreign update never waits on the lock of the owner.
  • save_document loads the row with session.get(LegalDocument, id, with_for_update=True), then checks ownership.
  • Each lock holds until commit or rollback.

Decided: one ownership rule, enforced under a row lock, with the existing error.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• E1. Ownership rule: a caller can write a row only when row.tenant_id is equal to the caller tenant. NULL is equal to NULL.
  • E1a. Tenant caller and shared row (NULL): treated as foreign. Tenant admins cannot edit shared documents.
  • E1b. No-tenant caller (system, ETL) and tenant row: treated as foreign.
  • E1c. No-tenant caller insert: the new row is shared (tenant_id NULL). This is the current behaviour, and it stays.
  • E1d. A no-tenant caller can write every shared row. Caller RBAC (admin role, ADR-0013) is the only guard on this path until RLS exists.
  • E2. Argument and context both set and different: the argument wins (T2).
  • E3. Payload has tenant_id on insert: the store ignores it and logs the key name as dropped (same as upsert today).
  • E4. save_document with a caller-chosen id that a foreign row owns: raise an error. Do not insert a new row with a new id. Do not overwrite.
  • E5. Empty-string tenant ("") in the argument or in the context: the store treats it as None (T2). An argument "" falls back to the context tenant. It never widens access beyond the context tenant.
  • E6. Payload without id: the store makes a new UUID4. No foreign row can own it, so the call inserts.

Decided: foreign rows behave like missing rows on update, and the upsert of a foreign id raises.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• F1. Cross-tenant update_document: raise StoreDocumentNotFoundError with the text Document not found: <id>, the same as for a missing id. The row stays unchanged. No commit happens.
  • F2. Cross-tenant save_document upsert: raise StoreDocumentNotFoundError with the text Document not found: <id>. The row stays unchanged. The payload dict stays unchanged (no new id, no other key). Parity with a missing id does not apply here, because a missing id inserts (see F4).
  • F3. StoreDocumentNotFoundError must be caught by except KeyError (T3). Change its base to KeyError. except LookupError in reject callers keeps working, because KeyError is a LookupError.
  • F4. Residual existence oracle on save_document: an unknown caller-chosen id inserts, a foreign id raises. The global primary key makes this unavoidable without RLS. The owner accepted this risk. Follow-up: server-generated ids only, so a caller cannot choose an id.
  • F5. Race: two inserts of the same new id at the same time. Both lookups miss, so both insert. The second raises IntegrityError from the database. This stays, and a test keeps it.
  • F6. No log line contains the caller tenant, the row tenant, the document id or payload values. The dropped-key warning logs the operation name and the key names only.
  • F7. StaleDataError on flush (the row changed or went away under the session): the store maps it to StoreDocumentNotFoundError with the same text. The session rolls back.
  • F8. Race between ownership check and write: closed by the row lock (T7).

Decided: one error type (StoreDocumentNotFoundError, now a KeyError) for "no row you can write".

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• M1. 100% of the QA cases pass (16 cases in qa.md), on the Docker PostgreSQL.
  • M2. 0 changed columns on the foreign row after each failed call (the test compares all 10 doc_to_dict fields before and after).
  • M3. update_document: the error type and text for a foreign id and a missing id are byte-equal in 100% of the cases.
  • M3a. save_document, measured separately: a foreign id raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError with the text Document not found: <id> in 100% of the cases. A missing id inserts one row in 100% of the cases.
  • M4. 0 regressions in the existing store tests (pytest -m "not integration" and the Docker integration suite).
  • M5. Coverage and mutation scores on the changed lines meet the CONTRIBUTING.md gates (no gate lowered).

docs.title: Tasks: tenant write guard (path 1, accepted)
docs.text:
Gate before build: the solution-architect checks contract.md against the current code.

  1. Find callers. List every call of save_document and update_document, and every except KeyError or except LookupError around them, in src/, scripts/ and tests/. Done when: the list is in the PR body, and each caller that relies on a payload tenant_id has a fix in task 4.
  2. Write tests first for QA-1 to QA-16 in qa.md, as integration tests on the Docker PostgreSQL. Done when: the new tests fail on main for every case except QA-8, QA-9 and QA-14 (current behaviour already passes them).
  3. Change the error. StoreDocumentNotFoundError gets base KeyError and a plain __str__. Done when: QA-12 and the existing reject tests pass.
  4. Add _resolve_tenant (with "" to None), _owned_row_for_update and _require_writable. Apply the row locks of requirement T7:
  5. update_document loads through _owned_row_for_update (id AND tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM tenant, FOR UPDATE).
  6. save_document loads with session.get(..., with_for_update=True), then calls _require_writable.
  7. Both map StaleDataError on flush to StoreDocumentNotFoundError.
  8. The dropped-key warning logs the operation name and key names only, with no document id.
  9. On insert, a payload tenant_id is dropped and logged by name.
  10. Update both docstrings, and state the shared-row guard limit. Fix the callers from task 1. Done when: QA-1 to QA-16 pass.
  11. Run the quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, pytest -m "not integration", the Docker suite, and the coverage and mutation gates. Done when: all pass with no gate lowered.

Order: tasks 1 and 2 in parallel, then 3, then 4, then 5. Follow-up (separate issue): server-generated ids only, so a caller cannot choose a document id.

docs.title: Path 1: ORM load-then-check (accepted)
docs.text: Lens: load the row under a lock, then check ownership. Writes stay ORM attribute writes through apply_update.

docs.title: Changes (all in postgres.py, mappers.py unchanged)
docs.text:
• StoreDocumentNotFoundError(KeyError): base changes from LookupError to KeyError. Add __str__ that returns the plain message, because str(KeyError("x")) adds quotes.
  • _resolve_tenant(tenant_id: str | None) -> str | None: "" becomes None, then the argument wins over get_current_tenant(). It never reads the payload.
  • _owned_row_for_update(session, document_id, tenant) -> LegalDocument: SELECT ... WHERE id AND tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM tenant FOR UPDATE. Raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError when no eligible row exists.
  • _require_writable(row: LegalDocument | None, document_id: str, tenant: str | None) -> LegalDocument: raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError(f"Document not found: {document_id}") when the row is None or row.tenant_id != tenant.
  • update_document: resolve, _owned_row_for_update, apply_update, commit.
  • save_document: resolve, session.get(..., with_for_update=True). None inserts with tenant_id=tenant. A foreign row raises through _require_writable. An owned row goes to apply_update. document["id"] is written only after the check passes. On insert, a payload tenant_id joins the dropped-key list.
  • Both: StaleDataError on flush maps to StoreDocumentNotFoundError. The dropped-key warning logs the operation name and key names only.

docs.title: Error flow
docs.text: The check runs before any attribute write. On a raise, the session rolls back, so the row is unchanged.

docs.title: Fit
docs.text:
• T2, E1, E3, E5: met by _resolve_tenant and the two ownership helpers.
  • F1-F3, F7, F8: met.
  • F4, F5: not handled (accepted, F5 kept by a test).

Effort: S.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
1. Race between check and write: closed by the row locks. A foreign update never waits on the lock of the owner. A foreign upsert through save_document can wait on it.
  2. The guard lives in Python only. A future write path that skips the helpers is unguarded. Mutation tests must keep the helper calls alive.

docs.title: Path 2: set-based conditional SQL
docs.text: Lens: the tenant predicate lives in one SQL statement per write. There is no read-then-write in Python.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• mappers.build_update_values(document) -> tuple[dict, list[str]] replaces apply_update. It maps allowlisted keys to columns and returns (values, sorted dropped keys).
  • _resolve_tenant(tenant_id: str | None) -> str | None: same rule as path 1.
  • _update_owned(session, doc_id, tenant, values) -> bool: UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM :tenant RETURNING id.
  • _upsert_owned(session, doc_id, tenant, insert_values, update_values) -> bool: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET ... WHERE legal_document.tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM :tenant RETURNING id.
  • save_document and update_document: zero rows returned means missing or foreign. Both raise StoreDocumentNotFoundError("Document not found: <id>").
  • StoreDocumentNotFoundError(KeyError): base change only.

docs.title: Error flow
docs.text: Zero rows means no commit. The row is unchanged.

docs.title: Fit
docs.text:
• T2, E1, E5: the resolved tenant is a bound parameter. IS NOT DISTINCT FROM gives NULL == NULL.
  • F1-F3: met. Check and write are one atomic statement (no race window).
  • F4: unchanged and accepted.
  • F5: changed. Two inserts of the same new id give no IntegrityError. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE makes the second call an update when both callers have the same tenant. When the tenants differ, the conflict WHERE fails and the second call raises StoreDocumentNotFoundError.

Effort: M. Two write paths rewritten, mapper changes shape, apply_update tests migrate.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
1. PostgreSQL-only SQL. Unit tests that do not use PostgreSQL move to the integration marker.
  2. Core statements skip the ORM unit of work. ORM defaults, onupdate hooks and JSON type coercion need a check.
  3. An empty values dict makes UPDATE ... SET invalid. It needs a fallback (SET id = id or an ownership SELECT).
  4. Insert and update value sets can drift apart.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The worker lifecycle issue asked workers to migrate once and close the store on exit. The RLS hardening change already moved migrations to the compose init service (lawbyai_owner). Workers only check the schema head. The open gap: no code closes the per-child PostgreSQLStore in src/tasks/fetch.py, and a comment there still says the store migrates.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• P1 local handler: module-level _store and a worker_process_shutdown handler in fetch.py. Effort S.
  • P2 central registry: src/tasks/lifecycle.py with close_all() wired in celery_app.py. Effort M.
  • P3 Celery Task base class: lazy store property and close_store(), bind=True. Effort S.
  • P4 storage provider: get_store() / close_store() in postgres.py. Effort S-M.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: P1, chosen by the user. - fetch.py replaces functools.cache with a module-level _store: PostgreSQLStore | None. _make_store() builds it lazily inside a task. - _close_store(**_: object) is connected to worker_process_shutdown. Empty cache: return, build nothing. Else call close() once, log a warning with exc_info on error, clear _store in finally. - The stale migration comment is corrected. No migration, role or celery_app.py change. - A failed build (for example SchemaNotAtHeadError) leaves _store as None, so the next task tries again (dba review). - Tests: 6 unit tests (no DB, no network) and 1 integration test on live PostgreSQL. The integration test saves old_pool = store._engine.pool after one query, asserts old_pool.checkedin() > 0, sends the signal, then asserts old_pool.checkedin() == 0, store._engine is None and _store is None (architect review: checkedout() == 0 cannot fail). - Handler signature _close_store(**_: object) with global _store. Unit tests reset _store in an autouse fixture.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Smallest diff: one source file. No change to the fetch_document signature.
  • The signal fires only in prefork children (also on max_tasks_per_child recycle). The solo pool, the threads pool and eager mode never fire it. Celery does not guarantee it, and a cold shutdown or hard kill can skip or cut it. Process exit then frees the sockets. Accepted risk.
  • A future task module with its own store needs its own handler. Extract a shared provider (P4) when a second consumer exists.
  • The dba review is light: no schema, migration or role change.
  • The worker lifecycle issue text must be updated to drop the migration scope.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• Each Celery worker child releases its PostgreSQL connections when it exits, so restarts and autoscale do not leave idle connections on a 4-6 GB host.
  • The code and comments match the RLS hardening change: workers never migrate. The init service runs alembic upgrade head as lawbyai_owner.
  • Decided: migration work is dropped from the worker lifecycle issue. The issue text is updated to say the RLS hardening change delivered it.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13, Celery prefork pool, SQLAlchemy engine inside PostgreSQLStore.
  • The store stays lazy: _make_store runs only inside a task, never at import time or in the parent process.
  • Close uses the Celery worker_process_shutdown signal only. No atexit fallback (user decision).
  • Files: src/tasks/fetch.py (and src/tasks/celery_app.py only if the handler belongs there). No migration or role change.
  • Quality gate: ruff, pyright, pytest -m "not integration", diff-cover 90%, Docker suite, mutation gate.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• A child that never ran a task has no cached store: the handler creates no PostgreSQLStore and opens no connection.
  • A child that ran many tasks has one store: the handler calls close() once.
  • After close, the cache is cleared, so a later call in the same process builds a new store, not a closed one.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• store.close() raises: the handler logs a warning with the traceback and returns. The child exits normally.
  • Celery skips the signal (hard kill, crash): process exit frees the sockets. Accepted risk, documented.
  • Schema behind head: unchanged; initialize() raises SchemaNotAtHeadError on first task.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 100% of unit tests for the handler pass with no database and no network.
  • 1 integration test on live PostgreSQL: after the handler runs, the saved old pool goes from more than 0 checked-in connections to 0, the store engine is None and the cache is empty.
  • 0 calls to PostgreSQLStore() when the handler runs in a child with no store.
  • 1 call to close() per child that has a store.
  • diff-cover >= 90% on changed lines. Mutation score meets the CONTRIBUTING.md gate.

docs.title: Path 1: local handler
docs.text:
• Structure: src/tasks/fetch.py only. Module-level _store: PostgreSQLStore | None replaces functools.cache. _close_store(**kwargs) is connected with @worker_process_shutdown.connect. Fix the stale migration comment.
  • Contract: kwargs ignored, returns None, never raises. Empty cache: no store built. Else close() once in try/except, warning with exc_info, finally clears the cache.
  • Unit tests: 0 constructions with empty cache; 1 close() after many _make_store(); close raises -> warning, cache empty; new instance after close; signal send triggers handler.
  • Integration: real store, one query, send signal, saved engine has pool.checkedout() == 0, cache empty.
  • Main risk: receiver connects only when tasks.fetch is imported (include=["tasks.fetch"] ensures it). A future task module with its own cache needs its own handler.
  • Effort: S (about 15 lines, one file).

docs.title: Path 2: central lifecycle registry
docs.text:
• Structure: new src/tasks/lifecycle.py with register_closable(name, peek, close) and close_all(). celery_app.py connects one worker_process_shutdown handler that calls close_all(). fetch.py registers peek/close for its module-level _store at import.
  • Contract: close_all() skips entries whose peek() is None; else close() once; errors logged as warning and swallowed, other entries still run; cache cleared in finally; re-register replaces.
  • Unit tests: as path 1, plus failing entry does not block others, re-register replaces, signal wiring.
  • Integration: real store, signal, pool.checkedout() == 0, cache empty.
  • Main risk: more machinery than one store needs (no second consumer yet). Wider diff-cover and mutation surface. Touches celery_app.py.
  • Effort: M (new module, two edits, about 8 unit tests + 1 integration).

docs.title: Path 3: task-owned resource (Celery Task base)
docs.text:
• Structure: fetch.py only. class _StoreTask(celery.Task) with lazy store property and close_store(). fetch_document uses base=_StoreTask, bind=True and reads self.store. A worker_process_shutdown handler calls fetch_document.close_store(). functools.cache removed.
  • Contract: first .store builds one store; close_store() with none cached builds nothing; else clears _store first, then close() once, warning on error.
  • Unit tests: as path 1, with patches on the property or _store. Existing fetch_document tests change for bind=True.
  • Integration: real store via .store, signal, pool.checkedout() == 0, _store is None.
  • Main risk: bind=True changes the task signature for direct calls in tests; every _make_store patch must change.
  • Effort: S (one file plus test edits; Celery's documented pattern).

docs.title: Path 4: per-process provider in storage layer
docs.text:
• Structure: get_store() / close_store() with module-level _store and a threading.Lock next to PostgreSQLStore in postgres.py. fetch.py calls get_store(). celery_app.py connects the shutdown handler to close_store().
  • Contract: get_store() returns one process-wide store, built lazily. close_store() never raises; none cached -> no build; else clear first, close() once, warning on error. Twice -> close once.
  • Unit tests: as path 1, plus double close, autouse reset fixture for the module global.
  • Integration: real store, close_store(), pool.checkedout() == 0, cache None.
  • Main risk: moves scope into the storage layer and celery_app.py (a requirements exception). Module global in a shared module can leak between tests. Reuse by Streamlit is speculative today.
  • Effort: S-M (about 25 lines across 3 files).

docs.title: QA-001 Child with no store closes nothing
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 1, Success Metric 3, T1
  • Type: edge
  • Given a Celery prefork child that has run 0 tasks and holds no database store
  • When the child receives the worker process shutdown signal
  • Then 0 new database stores are created and 0 database connections are opened

docs.title: QA-002 Child with one store closes it once
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 2, Success Metric 4, T1
  • Type: functional
  • Given a child that ran 50 fetch tasks and holds 1 store
  • When the child receives the worker process shutdown signal
  • Then the store is closed exactly 1 time

docs.title: QA-003 Store is rebuilt after close
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 3, T2
  • Type: functional
  • Given a child whose store was closed by the shutdown signal
  • When the same process runs one more fetch task
  • Then a second, new store is built (2 builds in total) and it is not the closed one

docs.title: QA-004 Close failure is logged and does not escape
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 1, T1
  • Type: failure
  • Given a child whose store raises RuntimeError("socket gone") on close
  • When the child receives the worker process shutdown signal
  • Then 1 warning with the traceback is logged, no error reaches the caller, and the child exits normally

docs.title: QA-005 Store is dropped even when close fails
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 1, Edge Case 3
  • Type: failure
  • Given a child whose store raises RuntimeError("socket gone") on close
  • When the shutdown signal is sent and then 1 new fetch task runs
  • Then the new task builds a fresh store (1 new build)

docs.title: QA-006 Hard kill skips the signal
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 2
  • Type: failure
  • Given a child that holds 1 store with 2 idle connections
  • When the child is killed with SIGKILL, so the signal never fires
  • Then the operating system closes the sockets at process exit and the database shows 0 connections from that child within 30 seconds. OPEN: the requirement gives no time limit, so 30 seconds is assumed.

docs.title: QA-007 Schema behind head fails on first task
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 3
  • Type: failure
  • Given a database whose schema is 1 revision behind head
  • When a child runs its first fetch task
  • Then the task fails with a schema-not-at-head error and no migration runs

docs.title: QA-008 Failed build is retried by the next task
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 3, T1
  • Type: failure
  • Given the first store build fails with a schema-not-at-head error and the schema is then upgraded to head
  • When the same child runs a second fetch task
  • Then the second task builds a store and completes, and no failed store stays cached

docs.title: QA-009 Shutdown after failed build closes nothing
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 3, T1
  • Type: edge
  • Given a child whose only store build failed
  • When the child receives the worker process shutdown signal
  • Then 0 close calls happen and no error is raised

docs.title: QA-010 Live pool is released
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 2, T3
  • Type: functional
  • Given a child that built a store on live PostgreSQL and ran 1 query, so the pool shows more than 0 checked-in connections
  • When the worker process shutdown signal is sent
  • Then the saved old pool shows 0 checked-in connections, the store has no engine, and the cached store is empty

docs.title: QA-011 Unit tests need no database or network
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 1, T2
  • Type: performance
  • Given the 6 handler unit tests and a machine with no PostgreSQL and no network
  • When the tests run with the non-integration marker
  • Then 6 of 6 pass (100%) and 0 connections are attempted

docs.title: QA-012 Shutdown signal reaches the handler
docs.text:
• Covers: T2, Technical Constraints
  • Type: functional
  • Given the task module is imported and 1 store is cached
  • When the worker process shutdown signal is sent with no sender
  • Then the store is closed exactly 1 time

docs.title: QA-013 Repeated shutdown signal is safe
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 1, Edge Case 2
  • Type: edge
  • Given a child with 1 store that already received the shutdown signal once
  • When the shutdown signal is sent a second time
  • Then no second close happens (1 close in total) and no error is raised

docs.title: QA-014 Importing the module opens no connection
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (lazy store)
  • Type: edge
  • Given a parent worker process and an unreachable database
  • When the task module is imported
  • Then 0 stores are built and 0 connections are attempted

docs.title: QA-015 Handler tolerates extra signal arguments
docs.text:
• Covers: T1
  • Type: edge
  • Given a child with 1 store
  • When the shutdown signal is sent with pid=4242, exitcode=0 and sender="ForkPoolWorker-3"
  • Then the store is closed exactly 1 time and no argument error occurs

docs.title: QA-016 Stale migration claim removed
docs.text:
• Covers: Business Goal 2, T1
  • Type: functional
  • Given the fetch task module after the change
  • When a reviewer searches it for the word "migrat"
  • Then 0 lines claim that the store migrates, and any match says the init service migrates

docs.title: QA-017 Worker never migrates
docs.text:
• Covers: Business Goal 2, Technical Constraints
  • Type: security
  • Given a database at head and a worker started with the application role
  • When the worker runs 1 fetch task
  • Then 0 schema change statements run and the application role is not given owner rights

docs.title: QA-018 Solo pool does not fire the signal
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints, decision Consequences
  • Type: edge
  • Given a worker started with the solo pool that built 1 store
  • When the worker runs a task and stops
  • Then the signal does not fire and the store is not closed by the handler. This is an accepted risk.

docs.title: QA-019 Child recycle closes the store
docs.text:
• Covers: Business Goal 1, decision Consequences
  • Type: functional
  • Given a prefork worker with a limit of 10 tasks per child and 1 child that ran 10 tasks
  • When the child is recycled
  • Then its old store is closed 1 time and the new child holds 0 stores until its first task

docs.title: QA-020 Autoscale shrink releases connections
docs.text:
• Covers: Business Goal 1
  • Type: performance
  • Given a worker with autoscale 4 to 1 and 4 children that each hold 3 idle connections (12 in total)
  • When autoscale stops 3 children
  • Then the database shows 3 connections from the remaining child and 0 from the stopped children

docs.title: QA-021 Coverage and mutation gate
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 5, T2
  • Type: performance
  • Given the change to the fetch task module and its 7 new tests
  • When the diff coverage and mutation checks run
  • Then diff coverage on changed lines is at least 90% and the mutation score meets the CONTRIBUTING.md gate

docs.title: worker-189 QA results
docs.text:
Unit run: .venv/bin/pytest -m "not integration" -> 1244 passed, 95 deselected. Docker integration suite (separate compose project, fresh volumes): 1334 passed, 5 skipped (4 need SEJM_LIVE_TEST=1, 1 needs the smoke worker). QA-010 is not among the skipped tests. ruff/pyright: not needed, because this run changed no Python file. No new tests written. docs.title: T1: module-level store and close handler
Context
docs.text: Each Celery prefork child builds one PostgreSQLStore but nothing closes it on exit. Idle connections stay open on a 4-6 GB host. This task serves the requirement to release connections at child exit and to fix the stale comment that says the store migrates (the RLS hardening change moved migration to the init service).

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: Edit only src/tasks/fetch.py. Design P1 from decision.md. - Remove import functools. Add from celery.signals import worker_process_shutdown. - Add module-level _store: PostgreSQLStore | None = None. - _make_store(): if _store is None, set _store = PostgreSQLStore(). Return it. A failed build (for example SchemaNotAtHeadError) leaves _store as None, so the next task retries. Call only inside a task. - Add _close_store(**_: object) -> None with global _store, connected with @worker_process_shutdown.connect. If _store is None: return, build nothing. Else call _store.close() once inside try. On Exception, _log.warning("store close failed", exc_info=True). In finally, set _store = None. - Replace the stale comment: workers never migrate, the init service runs alembic upgrade head, and the store only checks the schema head. - No change to celery_app.py, fetch_document signature, migrations or roles.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: child with no store
  Given _store is None
  When the worker_process_shutdown signal is sent
  Then PostgreSQLStore is not called and _store is None

Scenario: child with a store
  Given _store holds a store
  When the worker_process_shutdown signal is sent
  Then store.close is called once and _store is None

Scenario: close raises
  Given _store holds a store whose close raises
  When the worker_process_shutdown signal is sent
  Then a warning with exc_info is logged, no exception escapes and _store is None

Scenario: failed build
  Given PostgreSQLStore() raises
  When _make_store is called
  Then the error propagates and _store is None

Scenario: stale comment
  When grep -n 'migrat' src/tasks/fetch.py runs
  Then no line claims that the store migrates

docs.title: T3: integration test on live PostgreSQL
Context
docs.text: Unit tests use mocks. They cannot prove that the real SQLAlchemy pool releases its connections. This task serves the success metric: after the handler runs, the old pool goes from more than 0 checked-in connections to 0.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: Create tests/integration/tasks/test_fetch_close_store.py. Use production collaborators and live PostgreSQL. Mock nothing. - Reset tasks.fetch._store = None before and after. - Call _make_store(), run one query (for example a store read method), and save old_pool = store._engine.pool. - Assert old_pool.checkedin() > 0. - Send worker_process_shutdown.send(sender=None). - Assert old_pool.checkedin() == 0, store._engine is None and tasks.fetch._store is None. Do not assert checkedout() == 0: it cannot fail (architect review). - Follow the fixtures and markers of the other tests in tests/integration/. The schema must be at head (the init service does this).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: PostgreSQLStore.initialize() builds its engine with the default QueuePool (5 + 10). Each Celery prefork child caches its own store. With --concurrency=2, the worker can open 30 connections. The stack must fit in 4-6 GB RAM. See requirements.md.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: the caller passes a PoolConfig to PostgreSQLStore. The worker passes 1 + 1. The app uses the default 5 + 10.
  • Path 2: a PROCESS_ROLE setting selects the pool inside the store. Compose sets the worker role.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Path 1, chosen by the owner at the design gate. The solution architect and the DBA reviewed both paths and prefer Path 1.

Design points from the reviews: 1. src/config/settings.py: add one helper _int_at_least(name, default, minimum). An unset or empty value gives the default. A value that is not an integer, or that is below the minimum, raises ValueError and names the variable. The existing _positive helper stays as it is: it also parses floats and has 9 callers, and a change to it is outside this issue. 2. src/config/settings.py: add a frozen dataclass PoolConfig(size, max_overflow). __post_init__ raises ValueError when size < 1 or max_overflow < 0. Add the properties postgres_pool_size (default 5), postgres_max_overflow (default 10), worker_postgres_pool_size (default 1) and worker_postgres_max_overflow (default 1). Add app_pool_config() and worker_pool_config(). 3. src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py: PostgreSQLStore.__init__ gets a keyword-only pool: PoolConfig | None = None and does not read the settings. initialize() uses pool, or get_settings().app_pool_config() when it is None. It calls create_engine(url, future=True, pool_size=..., max_overflow=..., pool_pre_ping=True, pool_timeout=30). 4. src/tasks/fetch.py: _make_store() builds PostgreSQLStore(pool=get_settings().worker_pool_config()). 5. docker/docker-compose.yml: pass POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE and POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW in x-app-env. Pass WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE and WORKER_POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW on celery-worker. Add the four variables to docker/.env.example.

  1. The _int_at_least docstring states that an empty value gives the default, unlike _positive, which raises on an empty value. Both behaviors are intended.
  2. Add the four variables to the variable table in the settings.py module docstring. Export PoolConfig in __all__.
  3. Compose uses bare keys (NAME:). docker/.env.example lists the four variables commented out with their defaults. x-app-env also goes to celery-worker and test, so the worker sees the app values too. This is harmless, because the worker reads only the WORKER_* pair. init uses only x-db-env, so it gets the code defaults.
  4. In initialize(), the pool config is resolved before create_engine is called.
  5. The only store builder in src/tasks is _make_store (checked with grep: other builders are only in src/ui/components/auth.py and src/bootstrap/init_stack.py). One integration test runs fetch_document with a 1 + 1 pool.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• Settings.worker_pool_config() and Settings.app_pool_config(): no input. They return a PoolConfig. They raise ValueError that names the variable.
  • PoolConfig(size: int, max_overflow: int): raises ValueError for size < 1 or max_overflow < 0.
  • PostgreSQLStore(on_document_deleted=None, *, pool=None): never raises for the pool.
  • PostgreSQLStore.initialize(): for the app store, a bad setting raises ValueError before any engine exists. SchemaNotAtHeadError behavior does not change.
  • _make_store(): a bad WORKER_* value raises ValueError here, before initialize(). _store stays None, so the next task tries again.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The worker opens at most 4 connections with --concurrency=2 (was 30).
  • pool_pre_ping adds one round trip on each checkout. A worker child then survives a Postgres restart.
  • The init bootstrap service uses the app pool. It is short-lived, so this is accepted.
  • Risk: a new worker caller that builds PostgreSQLStore() directly gets the app pool. A test asserts that the fetch task gets its store only from _make_store.
  • Not in scope (follow-up): lower the app default (about 3 + 2) and tune Postgres memory (max_connections about 30, shared_buffers about 32 MB) for the 128 MB container limit.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• The stack runs on a host with 4-6 GB RAM. Each PostgreSQL connection costs memory on the server.
  • Today one Celery worker with --concurrency=2 can open up to 30 connections (2 children x (5 + 10)). Streamlit adds up to 15 more.
  • Goal: the worker opens at most 4 connections (2 children x (1 + 1)). The Streamlit app keeps a pool size that the operator can set.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13, SQLAlchemy 2.x create_engine with the default QueuePool.
  • PostgreSQLStore.initialize() builds the engine from get_settings(). Settings are os.getenv properties on Settings.
  • The worker builds its store lazily inside a task, after fork (src/tasks/fetch.py). No engine exists in the parent before fork.
  • The new settings: POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE (default 5), POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW (default 10), WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE (default 1), WORKER_POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW (default 1).
  • No new dependency. No migration. The architecture does not change.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• pool_size=0 makes a QueuePool unlimited in SQLAlchemy 2.x. The settings must reject a value lower than 1.
  • SQLAlchemy documents max_overflow=-1 as no overflow limit. The settings must reject a value lower than 0, so the pool is never unlimited.
  • A value that is not an integer (for example "abc") must raise a clear ValueError that names the variable.
  • An empty or unset variable uses the default.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• A bad pool value fails at engine build time with a ValueError that names the variable. It never falls back silently to an unlimited pool.
  • When all worker connections are busy, a task waits for the pool timeout (30 s default) and then fails. The failed task is persisted by the existing failure path (ADR-0006).
  • The Streamlit app is not affected by the worker settings.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• The worker engine has pool.size() == 1 and an overflow of 1 with the default settings: 1 unit test.
  • The app engine has pool.size() == 5 and an overflow of 10 with the default settings: 1 unit test.
  • Each of the 4 settings has a test for the default, a valid override and a rejected value: at least 12 cases.
  • With --concurrency=2, the worker opens at most 4 connections (down from 30).
  • Gate: ruff, pyright, fast tests, diff-cover 90% or more on the changed lines, Docker suite, CI mutation gate.

docs.title: Core idea
docs.text: PostgreSQLStore takes an optional frozen PoolConfig(size, max_overflow) through its constructor. Each caller picks the pool. The worker passes the worker pair. The Streamlit app uses the default, which is the app pair.

docs.title: Changed files
docs.text:
• src/config/settings.py: add a helper _int_in_range(name, default, minimum). Add 4 properties (db_pool_size, db_max_overflow, worker_db_pool_size, worker_db_max_overflow). Add app_pool_config() and worker_pool_config(). Define PoolConfig here, because postgres.py already imports the settings.
  • src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py: __init__ gets a keyword-only pool: PoolConfig | None = None. initialize() passes pool_size and max_overflow to create_engine. When pool is None, initialize() uses app_pool_config().
  • src/tasks/fetch.py: _make_store() builds PostgreSQLStore(pool=get_settings().worker_pool_config()).
  • src/ui/components/auth.py and src/bootstrap/init_stack.py: no change.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• _int_in_range returns an int. Unset or empty gives the default. A value that is not an integer raises ValueError and names the variable. A value below the minimum raises ValueError and names the variable. The minimum is 1 for the size and 0 for the overflow.
  • PoolConfig.__post_init__ checks size >= 1 and max_overflow >= 0.
  • PostgreSQLStore.__init__ does not read the settings. initialize() raises ValueError before it builds the engine. The SchemaNotAtHeadError path does not change.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Settings: 4 variables x (default, override, rejected) = 12 cases or more. Exact boundaries for the mutation gate.
  • The worker store engine has size 1 and overflow 1. The default store engine has size 5 and overflow 10.
  • _make_store passes the worker pair.
  • A bad value raises ValueError and leaves the store uninitialized.

docs.title: Effort
docs.text: S. Four files. No dependency, no migration.

docs.title: Main risk
docs.text: A new caller that builds PostgreSQLStore() in a worker gets the app pool. Mitigation: a test asserts that the worker uses _make_store.

docs.title: Core idea
docs.text: PostgreSQLStore keeps its no-argument constructor. initialize() reads the pool values from the settings. A new PROCESS_ROLE setting (app or worker) selects the pair. Compose sets PROCESS_ROLE=worker only on the celery-worker service.

docs.title: Changed files
docs.text:
• src/config/settings.py: 4 int properties (DB_POOL_SIZE 5, DB_MAX_OVERFLOW 10, WORKER_DB_POOL_SIZE 1, WORKER_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW 1), one int-parse helper, and a process_role property (default app).
  • src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py: initialize() picks the pair by role and passes it to create_engine.
  • docker/docker-compose.yml: the celery-worker service gets PROCESS_ROLE=worker and passes the WORKER_* variables.
  • src/tasks/fetch.py: no change.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• Each int property returns an int. Unset or empty gives the default. A value that is not an integer, a size below 1 or an overflow below 0 raises ValueError and names the variable.
  • process_role returns app or worker. Any other value raises ValueError that names PROCESS_ROLE.
  • initialize() keeps its signature. It raises ValueError before it builds the engine.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Settings: 12 cases or more, plus the role values.
  • Store engine with the default role: size 5, overflow 10. With PROCESS_ROLE=worker: size 1, overflow 1.
  • A compose check that celery-worker carries the worker role.

docs.title: Effort
docs.text: S. Three files plus compose.

docs.title: Main risk
docs.text: The role is a deploy-time contract. A worker that starts without PROCESS_ROLE=worker (another compose file, a manual celery run) gets 5+10 again, and no code detects it. It also adds a fifth setting that the requirements do not list.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The worker must open at most 4 connections and the app pool must be settable. This task adds the settings layer that T2 and T3 use. It serves the goals and the edge cases in requirements.md (reject size < 1, overflow < 0, non-integer, empty uses default).

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
In src/config/settings.py: - Add _int_at_least(name, default, minimum). Unset or empty returns default. A non-integer or a value below minimum raises ValueError that names the variable. The docstring says an empty value gives the default, unlike _positive. Do not change _positive. - Add frozen dataclass PoolConfig(size, max_overflow). __post_init__ raises ValueError for size < 1 or max_overflow < 0. - Add properties postgres_pool_size (5, min 1), postgres_max_overflow (10, min 0), worker_postgres_pool_size (1, min 1), worker_postgres_max_overflow (1, min 0). Env names are POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE, POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW, WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE, WORKER_POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW. - Add app_pool_config() and worker_pool_config() that return a PoolConfig. - Add the four variables to the module docstring table. Export PoolConfig in __all__.

Tests in tests/unit/config/test_settings_pool.py (use monkeypatch.setenv and delenv). At least 12 cases: default, valid override and rejected value for each of the 4 settings.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: Defaults
  Given none of the four pool variables is set
  When app_pool_config() and worker_pool_config() are called
  Then app is PoolConfig(5, 10) and worker is PoolConfig(1, 1)

Scenario: Valid override
  Given WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE is "2" and POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW is "0"
  When the properties are read
  Then worker_postgres_pool_size is 2 and postgres_max_overflow is 0

Scenario: Empty value uses the default
  Given POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE is ""
  When postgres_pool_size is read
  Then it returns 5

Scenario Outline: Rejected value
  Given <name> is "<value>"
  When the matching property is read
  Then ValueError is raised and its message contains "<name>"
  Examples:
    | name                         | value |
    | POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE           | 0     |
    | POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW        | -1    |
    | WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE    | abc   |
    | WORKER_POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW | -1    |

Scenario: PoolConfig validates itself
  Given a PoolConfig is built with size 0 or with max_overflow -1
  When __post_init__ runs
  Then ValueError is raised in both cases

docs.title: T3: Worker store uses the worker pool
Context
docs.text: The Celery fetch task builds its store lazily in each prefork child. It must use the worker pool so the worker opens at most 4 connections with --concurrency=2. It depends on T2.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• src/tasks/fetch.py: _make_store() returns PostgreSQLStore(pool=get_settings().worker_pool_config()). The config is resolved before initialize(). On a ValueError, _store stays None.
  • Unit test tests/unit/tasks/test_fetch_store.py: (a) bad WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE makes _make_store() raise ValueError and fetch._store is still None, and a later call with a good value succeeds. (b) The fetch task gets its store only from _make_store: patch _make_store and assert the task calls it, and assert no other PostgreSQLStore( call exists in src/tasks/fetch.py (source check).
  • Integration test tests/integration/test_fetch_worker_pool.py, function test_fetch_document_worker_pool. Follow tests/integration/test_fetch_task_integration.py and conftest.py: use pytestmark = [pytest.mark.integration, pytest.mark.usefixtures("eager_celery")], the postgres_url fixture, the registries and source_url fixtures pattern (shared fakes from fakes.fetch), and reset fetch._store with monkeypatch. Set WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE=1 and WORKER_POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW=1. Mock only the network edge (the fake source). Use the real store. Assert fetch._store's engine pool.size() == 1, the max overflow is 1, and the stored row exists.
  • Resolved: assert the pool through SQLAlchemy introspection: pool.size() == 1, max overflow 1, and pool.checkedout() == 0 after the task. A pg_stat_activity count is not needed.

docs.text:
Scenario: Worker store uses the worker pool
  Given WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE is "1" and WORKER_POSTGRES_MAX_OVERFLOW is "1"
  When _make_store() is called
  Then the store receives PoolConfig(1, 1)

Scenario: Bad worker value
  Given WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE is "0" and fetch._store is None
  When _make_store() is called
  Then ValueError naming WORKER_POSTGRES_POOL_SIZE is raised and fetch._store is still None

Scenario: Retry after a bad value
  Given a previous _make_store() call failed on a bad value
  When the value is fixed and _make_store() is called again
  Then it returns a store and fetch._store is set after the next task

Scenario: Only _make_store builds the store
  Given the source of src/tasks/fetch.py
  When it is searched for PostgreSQLStore( calls
  Then the only call is inside _make_store

Scenario: fetch_document with a 1 + 1 pool
  Given a live PostgreSQL, a fake source and a 1 + 1 worker pool
  When fetch_document runs in eager mode
  Then the document row is stored, the engine has pool.size() 1 and overflow 1, and at most 2 connections are open
